analysis:
The PR changes only docs/architecture/inference.md. It bumps the 'Last updated' date (line 3) and adds one troubleshooting-table row (around head line 2316). The row says a cold load can be refused when an idle model is resident, because that slot holds an unexpired Autopilot placement hold. Held slots are excluded from eviction (ProviderLoop.evictableModelSlots, autopilotHoldsModel), and their weights get no free_for_load_gb reclaim credit (autopilotHeldWeightBytes). The row points to model-autopilot.md and ProviderLoop+AutopilotPlacement.swift. No source code, wire protocol, key handling, attestation, authorization or cache-storage code changes. The row is a documentation-only description of availability behavior.

I considered T-041 (prefix-cache tiers) and TB-007 (inference engine), the only retrieved definitions. The change does not touch the SSD tier, cacheSalt scoping, the TTL or the KEK purge points, so those mitigations are unaffected.

The visible head excerpt (lines 1-415) and the base excerpt (lines 2366-2597) do not contain the new row. The new row appears only in the patch excerpt, so I could not cite a visible line for it.

Open integration question: the Autopilot placement-hold feature and its source files are not in the supplied evidence. Whether holds can be abused by a consumer or provider to cause denial of service (a pre-existing or separate-PR concern) is unverified. That is not a regression in this documentation change. The threat model may eventually need an entry for placement-hold availability if that feature is new. No finding is supported by this PR's evidence.
